h: Conquering Sichon Opens the Way to an Honest Reckoning

p: What is meant by that which is written (Bamidbar 21:27),
"The rulers" — these are those who rule over their yetzer;
בּוֹאוּ וּנְחַשּׁוֹב חֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי
come and let us make the reckoning of the world, etc.
And it expounds the entire passage
Now this needs to be understood:
which is like the giving of a reason
what connection does this matter have
גַּם כָּל עִנְיַן מִלְחֲמוֹת סִיחוֹן וְעוֹג
Also, the whole matter of the wars of Sichon and Og,
who are called the two kings of the Emori
and the Emori is one of the seven nations;
so why was Moshe in doubt
for it appears that had Sichon allowed
Yisrael to pass through his border,
they would not have conquered him at all?
וְגַם בַּמִּשְׁנָה (בִּכּוּרִים פֶּרֶק א מִשְׁנָה י)
אֵין מְבִיאִין בִּכּוּרִים מֵעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן וְכוּלֵּי
bikkurim are not brought from across the Yarden, etc.;
נִרְאֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ כִּקְדוּשַּׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְגַמְרֵי
it appears that it does not have the full sanctity of Eretz Yisrael.
correspond to the seven middos in impurity,
which correspond to the seven middos in holiness.
And it is brought in the sefer Divrei Emes
from the Rebbe of Lublin, zecher tzaddik livrachah,
בְּשֵׁם הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory,
that the kelipah of the kingdom of the Emori,
which is the third of the seven nations,
corresponds to the middah of Tiferes in holiness.
אֶת ה׳ הֶאֱמַרְתָּ וַה׳ הֶאֱמִירְךָ (דְּבָרִים כו, יז–יח)
"You have exalted Hashem… and Hashem has exalted you" (Devarim 26:17–18),
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu is praised
וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And it corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
who was small and lowly in his own eyes,
"I have become small from all the kindnesses";
מִי יָקוּם יַעֲקֹב כִּי קָטֹן הוּא
"Who will raise up Yaakov, for he is small?"
also the holiness of Avraham and Yitzchak
(וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ תְּרוּמָה קעה, ב
(as it says in the holy Zohar, Terumah 175b,
And Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, knew
that it was not yet the time
וְכֵן אַף אַחַר כָּךְ מָצִינוּ (נְדָרִים כב, א–ב)
And so, even afterward, we find (Nedarim 22a–b):
"At that time we had not yet crossed the Yarden"
of the kelipah of jealousy and murder.
of what is written in Parashas Devarim (Devarim 1:4):
king of the Emori, who dwells in Cheshbon,
and Og, king of the Bashan,
for here it says "after he had smitten them,"
meaning that they left no soul alive.
there had not yet been completely uprooted
the entire kelipah of the Emori,
מַה שֶּׁהָיָה נִקְרָא מִתְּחִלָּה מֶלֶךְ חֶשְׁבּוֹן
that whereas he was at first called "king of Cheshbon,"
as he is called at first in Parashas Devarim…
That is, since his kelipah included
all three kelipos, as mentioned above,
he was king over the reckoning,
not allowing the reckoning to be made at all.
And in this respect Moshe Rabbeinu conquered him;
and he did not conquer it completely,
so that he still dwells in Cheshbon:
he is still able to entice people
not to make the reckoning of the world;
at the time of the yetzer hara
no one remembers the yetzer tov.
And Moav is the root of the kelipah of desire,
after a ravenous craving for forbidden relations,
in the end is made to eat of his own flesh.
And the essence of the kelipah was in Moav,
שֶׁקְּרָאַתּוּ מֵאָב (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ נָזִיר כג, ב)
whom she named "from father" (as they said, Nazir 23b).
And this is what it says afterward,
"For Cheshbon was the city of Sichon,
וְהוּא נִלְחַם בְּמֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב הָרִאשׁוֹן וְגוֹ׳
and he had fought against the former king of Moav, etc."
That is, Sichon was king of Cheshbon,
so that a person should not make at all
so that he would no longer be king of Cheshbon,
these are those who rule over their yetzer;
בּוֹאוּ וּנְחַשֵּׁב חֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵּי
come and let us make the reckoning of the world, etc.;
and established in the World to Come.
For once one merely begins to make
he is already able to rectify,
so that he is built and established
in this world and for the World to Come.
דְּסִיחוֹן נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם ב׳ הַקְּלִיפּוֹת
For Sichon is named after two of the kelipos,
דְּאַחַר כָּךְ דָּרַשׁ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא שָׁם)
since afterward the Gemara (Bava Basra 78b) expounds
"like a cedar in the Levanon he will grow tall,"
And in the kelipah he is called Sichon
that he raises his mind high like a cedar,
and he is further called Sichon
on account of the kelipah of desire,
in that he goes after pleasant talk,
which is the kelipah of desire,
"For the lips of a strange woman drip honey, etc.,
and her palate is smoother than oil."
But Og's kelipah was only arrogance,
this is Og, who escaped from the generation of the Flood.
The sin of the Flood was robbery and immorality,
which implies that he was not unbridled
in the kelipah of jealousy and desire,
and his kelipah was only arrogance.
This is not so of Sichon:
(as they said in the Gemara there, Niddah 61a),
that Sichon was born in the Ark
from the wife of Cham through immorality;
and he included all three kelipos,
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי נִקְרָא סִיחוֹן מֶלֶךְ חֶשְׁבּוֹן
That is why Sichon is called king of Cheshbon,
whereas Og's kelipah was only arrogance;
and both of them are called kings of the Emori.

p: And as for what is said regarding Og (Bamidbar 21:34),
and it is brought in the holy Zohar
סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (חֵלֶק ג קפד, א)
at the end of this parashah (Zohar III 184a):
the mark that Avraham had imprinted, etc.,
דְּהָא הוּא פָּגִים רְשִׁימָא דִּילֵיהּ וְכוּלֵּי
for he had blemished his mark, etc."
That is, since in truth he had not converted,
so as to be called by the name of Yisrael,
רַק שֶׁנִּימּוֹל בֵּין אַנְשֵׁי בֵּיתוֹ דְּאַבְרָהָם
but was only circumcised among the members of Avraham's household,
as it says in the holy Zohar.
That is, he was not one purchased with his money,
such that he would be obligated to circumcise him;
like all "the souls that they had made in Charan,"
and he was considered like the circumcised of the nations of the world,
for "the term 'orlah' is applied only to them"
And this is what it says,
שֶׁאַחַר פְּטִירַת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
after the passing of Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
all the souls that they had made in Charan
for he stood against the entire reckoning,
to prevent a person from reckoning at all.
then "the rulers said: Come and let us reckon"
for the words of the tzaddikim are effective,
those who rule over their yetzer,
to enter the hearts of those who hear their words,
when they say: Come and let us make
And if one merely begins to reckon,
then "it will be built and established"
in this world and for the World to Come,
so that it will be within his ability to rectify everything.
if a person makes himself like a young donkey
which is from the kelipah of desire,
"For a fire went out from Cheshbon, etc."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (עוֹבַדְיָה א, יח)
"And the house of Yaakov shall be fire,
and the house of Yosef a flame."
Yaakov corresponds to the kelipah of arrogance,
and Yosef is the middah of Tzaddik,
And this is what it says:
"Let a fire go out from those who reckon, etc.;
a flame from the city of Sichon"
from the city of the tzaddikim,
this is one who follows his yetzer
and that is the kelipah of desire,
"The lords of the high places of Arnon"
these are the haughty of spirit;
for the kelipah of Moav included arrogance as well,
"We have heard of the pride of Moav, exceedingly proud."
And the fire of the tzaddikim
is a fire that consumes fire,
so that it can thereby rectify
all three kelipos are called fire:
וְתַאֲוָה גַּם כֵּן נִקְרָא (קִידּוּשִׁין פא, א)
and desire too is called so (Kiddushin 81a):
"there came out, etc., a pillar of fire;
See that you are fire, etc."
וְגַאֲוָה הוּא גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ אֵשׁ
And arrogance too is like fire,
for the way of fire is to rise upward.
שֶׁזֶּה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ח, א)
and this is the meaning of what they said (Berachos 8a):
nine hundred and three kinds of death
That is, corresponding to three times "fire"
which take a person out of the world.
is a fire that consumes fire,
And this is: "If you do so"
that those who rule over their yetzer say
and it enters the hearts of the listeners
then "it will be built" in this world
"and established" for the World to Come,
so that all will be rectified.
And this is: "Let a fire go out from those who reckon
and consume those who do not reckon."
And the Gemara enumerates what it will rectify:
and that is why they are called Moav here,
because they came from this kelipah.
"The lords of the high places of Arnon"
וְזֶה שֶׁהֵבִיא אַחַר כָּךְ פָּסוּק (בְּמִדְבַּר כא, כט)
And this is why it afterward brings the pasuk (Bamidbar 21:29),
וְכָל פָּסוּק זֶה לֹא נִדְרַשׁ כְּלָל כָּאן
and this entire pasuk is not expounded at all here
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִקְשָׁה גַּם הַמַּהַרְשָׁ״א זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
as the Maharsha, of blessed memory, also asked.
even according to the allusive exposition,
נִתְפָּרֵשׁ גַּם כֵּן כִּפְשׁוּטוֹ עַל מוֹאָב
is also explained according to its plain meaning, about Moav,
and they became included in his kelipah,
"like a cedar in the Levanon he will grow tall,"
only the loftiness is in holiness,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים ב יז, ו)
"And his heart was lifted up in the ways of Hashem"
so that their fire can rectify
the fire of the kelipah of Moav as well.
"You are lost, O people of Kemosh":
only that they could not conquer them
is because of the two good doves
And this entire pasuk is explained according to its plain meaning
even according to the allusion alluded to here.
And afterward it says, "We have shot at them"
regarding one who has heresy in him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ אָמַר רָשָׁע אֵין רָם
as they said: the wicked one says, there is no One on high;
the reckoning of the world is lost,
there is no judgment and no Judge.
For such a wicked one it will not help
that those who rule over their yetzer say
come and let us reckon, etc."
that is, the fire of Gehinnom,
And on Shabbos, "the daughter is crowned with the Avos,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ וַיַּקְהֵל (חֵלֶק ב רד, א)
as it says in the holy Zohar, Vayakhel (Zohar II 204a);
the holiness of the three Avos,
who correspond to the three kelipos mentioned,
and he is able to come and make
which is a fire that consumes fire;
and he will be built in this world
and established for the World to Come.

paragraphs.text: Source: Esther 1:12 — “ותמאן המלכה ושתי לבוא בדבר המלך אשר ביד הסריסים ויקצף המלך מאד וחמתו בערה בו” — “But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s command conveyed by the eunuchs. The king was greatly incensed, and his fury burned within him.”

paragraphs.text: Source of the quoted words: Kiddushin 81a — “… אמרו ליה: כסיפתינן. אמר להו: מוטב תיכספו בי עמרם בעלמא הדין ולא תיכספו מיניה לעלמא דאתי. אשבעיה דינפק מיניה, נפק מיניה כי עמודא דנורא. אמר ליה: חזי, דאת נורא ואנא …” — “When he was halfway up the ladder, he strengthened his legs against the sides of the ladder to stop himself from climbing further, raised his voice, and cried out: There is a fire in the house of Amram. Upon hearing …”

paragraphs.text: Source of the quoted words: Bava Basra 78b — “״ונירם״ – אמר רשע: אין רם, ״אבד חשבון״ – אבד חשבונו של עולם; ״עד דיבן״ – אמר הקדוש ברוך הוא: המתן עד שיבא דין, ״ונשים” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 166) — “The Gemara interprets a subsequent verse: “We have shot at them [vanniram], Heshbon is perished, even until Dibon, and we have laid waste even until Nophah, which reaches until Medeba” (Numbers 21:30). “Vanniram”; this indicates that the wicked person says: …”

paragraphs.text: Source of the quoted words: Bava Basra 79a — “עד נפח״ – עד שתבא אש שאינה צריכה ניפוח, ״עד מידבא״ – עד שתדאיב נשמתן. ואמרי לה: עד דעביד מאי דבעי.” — “even until Nophah,” meaning until the fire comes that does not require fanning [nippuaḥ], i.e., the fire of Gehenna, which will consume them. “Until Medeba [Medeva]”; this means until their souls are pained [tadiv]. And some say an alternative explanation: …”
